statement: How many even numbers are there from 10 to 20, counting 10 and 20 too?

choices.misconception: I left out 10 and 20, the two numbers at the ends.
I counted the odd numbers, 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19.
I worked out 20 minus 10 instead of counting the even numbers.
I counted every number from 10 to 20, odd ones too.

hints: Even numbers go up in steps of 2. Start at 10, keep adding 2, and stop at 20. Count every number you say, including both ends.
Say them: 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20. Count them on your fingers.

solutions.reliable: Count in twos from 10: 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20. That is 6 even numbers. The idea to keep: list numbers by steps of 2 and include both ends when the question says so.
solutions.elegant: From 10 to 20 there are 11 numbers. They start and end with an even number and take turns even, odd, even, so the even ones are one more than the odd ones: 6 even and 5 odd. The idea to keep: when a list starts and ends on even, the evens win by one.

whyOnTest: Counting evens in a range tests the step-of-2 idea and the end-point trap together.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
